lawyer:
ABM Nurul Islam with Mahfuzur Rahman with Abdus Salam Mondal and Fara Mahmuda, Advocates — For the Petitioner 
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Additional Attorney-General with Mir Hashmat Ali, Assistant Attorney-General — For the Respondents
parties:
Aminul Ghani Titto (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh Election Commission represented by Chief Election Commissioner and another  ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Habibur Rahman Khan J : The petitioner Aminul Ghani Titto filed an application under Article 102(2)(ii) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh on 29.6.95 with a prayer for issuing a Rule Nisi upon the Respondents to show cause as to why they shall not be directed to delete/omit/withdraw/cancel/rescind the fixation of 1.1.95 as the date for determination of age of 18 years of a person for becoming a voter vide Annexure-A and also questioned the Press Release dated 28.5.95 issued by the Election Commissioner and published in the daily newspapers on 28.5.95 vide Annexure 'B' to the Writ Petition requiring the person to fill up the form at the place from where he desires to cast his vote. Subsequently on 19.6.95 the prayer having been amended at the instance of the petitioner on filing supplementary affidavit a Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why registration and enrolment of voters starting on and from 25.5.95 fixing qualifying date as on 1.1.95 with retrospective effect and failing to start the process of registration from 1.1.95 vide Annexure-A to the writ petition and directing the eligible voters including the petitioner to go to the place where he wants to vote for filling up from No. 2 in violation of serial No. 11 of the Form prepared and issued under the Electoral Rolls Rules, 1982 vide Annexure-B to the Writ Petition, shall not be declared to have been passed and made illegally without any lawful authority and, as such, are of no legal effect or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. In the writ petition it is stated, inter alia, that the petitioner is a citizen, and permanent resident of Bangladesh and he is an Advocate by profession being a member of Dhaka Bar Association. The petitioner hails from village Shantinagar, Union-Gayhata, PS Nagarpur, District Tangail where he has his house and immovable properties. For professional reasons he now temporarily resides at 12/5 F—Block, Joint Quarters, Mohammadpur, Dhaka-1207. The petitioner intends to contest in the forthcoming election of the Parliament from Nagarpur constituency under District Tangail. The petitioner also intends to cast his vote in Dhaka City Corporation Election and, as such, he needs to be a voter in the city of Dhaka. The petitioner needs to be registered as a voter in the Electoral Roll to be prepared for Parliament from Nagarpur constituency. It is submitted that under Article 122(2) of the Constitution no bar has been imposed debarring a citizen of Bangladesh aged over 18 years from registering himself as a voter in the Electoral Roll from more than one place, namely, from his permanent residence but there is no denying the fact that no voter can vote twice or more than once and in more than one electoral constituency or election centre. For the purpose of preparation of voter's list Election Commission issued certain directions and under paragraph 3.3. of the said direction the Election Commission fixed January 1, 1995 as the date on which a person, if attains the age of 18 years, will be entitled to be registered and enrolled as a voter. Though the qualifying date for registration of voters was fixed on 1st January, 1995 the Election Commission started registration of voters from 25th May 1995 for publishing the voters list finally on 31st August, 1995. The Election Commission prescribed, printed and published Form 2 according to rule 4 (3) of the Electoral Rolls Rules, 1982 for the purpose of preparing the Register of voters and the Electoral Roll for an electoral area, the Registration Officer shall cause to be obtained statement in Form-2 from each eligible voter who fulfills conditions laid down in clauses (a) to (d) of section 7 (1) of the Ordinance 1982. While filling up the Form No. 2 a person is to put tick mark indicating the place from where he wants to cast his vote for the election of Parliament, Union Parishad, Pourashava and City Corporation It is submitted that the Bangladesh Election Commission fixed 1-1-95 as the date for the purpose of determination of qualifying age of the voters but started the preparation of electoral rolls from 25-5-95 fixing 31-8-95 as the date for publishing the final voters list and by the said order a person who has attained eighteen years after 1.1.95 has been debarred from being registered and enrolled as a voter. In the supplementary affidavit while amending the prayer made in the main writ petition some more facts have been added submitting that under section 11(A) of the Electoral Roll Ordinance, 1982 the Election Commission was to issue identity card and for that purpose according to Form 2 prepared under Rule 4 of the Electoral Rolls Rules. 1982 it is required that at the time of filling up Form 2 the person intending to be enrolled as voter must affix his photo but no such photo of the petitioner, though offered, was taken by ,the enumerators or registration officers. 

 3. The Rule has been opposed by the Respondents who have filed affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit-in-opposition. It is submitted that according to Article 122 (1) the Election of Parliament shall be on the basis of adult franchise and clause (2) (d) of the said Article provides that "A person shall be entitled to be enrolled on the electoral roll for a constituency delimited for the purpose of election to parliament, if he is not less than eighteen years of age. According to section 3(e) of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance LXI of 1982) the qualifying date in relation to the preparation, amendment, or revision of every electoral roll under the Ordinance means the first day of January of the year in which electoral roll is so prepared or revised and as the preparation of electoral rolls started in 1995 in terms of the Article 122(2)(b) of the Constitution and Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 the Election Commission has fixed the qualifying age of person for becoming a voter on his attaining the age of eighteen years on 1.1.1995. 

 4. From the statements and averments made in the petition and the affidavits it transpires that the main grievances of the petitioner are two-fold. The first point initially raised by Mr. ABM Nurul Islam, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, was that though Article 122 prescribes that election to the Parliament shall be on the basis of adult franchise and under clause (2) (h) a person shall be enrolled on the Electoral Roll if he is not less than eighteen years of age and fixation of 1.1.95 as the qualifying date under the Ordinance and the direction of the Election Commission is ultra vires to the Constitution. 

 5. Having regard to the fact that the Constitution has not fixed any qualifying date and the provision of section 3(e) of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 fixing the qualifying age and date the learned Advocate for the petitioner found it difficult to substantiate his point challenging the vires of the statutory provision of law inasmuch as similar provision has been prevailing in our country since 1982 and are there in the neighboring countries of the Sub-Continent. Mr. Islam, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, took a different stand at a later stage of his argument and submitted that as section 7 of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 mandates that draft Electoral Roll shall be prepared in respect of the person attaining the age of eighteen years on the qualifying date the Commission was under obligation to start preparation of the electoral roll on 1-1-95 or soon thereafter. It is therefore, argued that the Election Commission started preparation of draft electoral roll and registration and enrollment of voters not on the qualifying date but on a much later date on 25th May 1995 in total ignorance and in violation of section 7 of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 and has thereby acted illegally and without any lawful authority resulting in the exclusion of few millions of eligible voters from being enrolled as electors and thus they will be deprived of their valuable right of franchise as guaranteed under Articles 119 and 122 of the Constitution. 

 6. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Additional Attorney-General appearing for the respondents, submitted that qualifying date in relation to the preparation, amendment or revision of every electoral roll means the first day of January of the year in which the electoral roll is prepared or revised as contemplated in the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982. It is further submitted that the electoral rolls may be amended, corrected or revised according to sections 10 and 11 of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 and a fresh electoral roll may be prepared if the Commission finds therein any gross irregularity under section 7(7) of the Ordinance and any person whose name has not been included in the roll may apply for enrolment under rule 20 of the Electoral Rolls Rules, 1982. It is further submitted that the qualifying date marking a particular date in the year when the election is held is an essential feature of the Ordinance whereby fixing a qualifying date in relation to the preparation, amendment and revision of the electoral roll on the first day of January of the year when the election is held has been done within the legislative competence and hence cannot be held as ultra vires to the Constitution. The learned Additional Attorney-General further argued that in every election previously held in this country and also in the adjoining countries in the Sub-Continent for the preparation of Electoral Roll the qualifying date is prescribed as a component part of election laws. In our country in the past in the Electoral Ordinance, 1972 (President's Order 100 of 1972) and in the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1974 and 1976 the qualifying date was fixed on 1st January of the year of election. The Representation of the Peoples Act 1950 (Act 43 of 1950) also contained similar provision of qualifying date in relation to the preparation or revision of electoral roll on the 1st day of January of the year in which the roll was prepared or revised. In this respect a number of decisions was cited by the learned Additional Attorney-General. The learned Advocate for the petitioner found it difficult to controvert the submission of the learned Additional Attorney-General by showing any law or citing any decided case. 

 7. In the case of AK Gopalan vs. The Election Commission of India and another reported in 1971 (Full Bench) page 39 it was observed "According to section 14 of that act qualifying date in relation to the preparation or revision of every electoral A means the 1st day of January of the year in which the roll is prepared or revised 

 8. In the case of Jyoti Basu and others vs. Debi Ghosal and others reported in AIR 1982 (SC) 983 it was observed "A right to elect, fundamental though it is to democracy, is, anomalously enough, neither a fundamental right nor a common Law Right. It is pure and simple, a statutory right. So is the right to be elected. So is the right to dispute an election. Outside of the statute, there is no right to elect, no right to be elected and no right to dispute an election, statutory creation they are, and therefore, subject to statutory limitation" The above view is in line with the well recognized principle of fixing the qualifying date having regard to the qualifying age as prescribed in the Constitution for the purpose of preparation of electoral roll or revision thereof. At a later stage Mr. Islam instead of pursuing his earlier submission challenging the vires of the Ordinance, turned his argument attacking the role of the Election Commission in not initiating the process of preparation of the electoral roll for the purpose of registration and enrollment of voters on 1st January, 1995 which has been prescribed as the qualifying date or soon thereafter. It is submitted that the Election Commission having started the work of preparation of the electoral roll at a belated stage on 25th May 1995 has acted illegally and without lawful authority as a result of which huge number of persons attaining the qualifying age of eighteen years subsequent to January 1995 have been excluded from being enlisted as voters and thereby will be debarred from exercising their valuable right of franchise in the ensuing election. The learned Additional Attorney-General found it difficult to controvert the above contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner though he remained firm in his stand that on the face of statutory provision regarding the qualifying age and date the petitioner is not entitled to any relief in the instant writ petition only for the reason that the process of preparation of electoral roll was started at a belated stage. This submission of the Additional Attorney-General bears substance as it gets support from the statutory provision of law. At the same time it cannot be altogether ignored that a great bulk of the population who have attained the qualifying age of eighteen years subsequent to 1st January 1995 which has been fixed as the qualifying date for the purpose of enrolment as voters are going to be deprived from exercising their right of franchise. In this regard before parting with the point we feel it our onerous duty to express our anxiety and pious wish that the Election Commission will keep its mind open to find out remedial measures for the inclusion of the persons who have attained the qualifying age of eighteen years after 1st January, 1995 which has been fixed as the qualifying date with reference to the qualifying age as enjoined in the Constitution as well as in the Ordinance, 1982, if permissible, and as and when occasion arises, taking recourse to the provision of section 7(2), section 10 and section 11 of the Electoral Rolls Ordinance, 1982 read with rule 20 of the Electoral Rolls Rules 1982 keeping in view the well-recognized principle that the preparation of Electoral Rolls is a continuing process. The above view taken by us is in line with the observation made by Lord Denning in his book "Discipline in Law" page 16, which reads as "It is no longer necessary for the Judges to wring their hands and say there is nothing we can do without it, whenever strict interference of statute gives rise to an absurd situation. The Judges can and should use good sense to remedy it by reading words in, if necessary, so as to what parliament would have done had they had the situation in mind". 

 9. In this regard the learned Additional Attorney-General submitted that since the registration of voters is to be made on the basis of house-to-house verification and services each voter is to remain present at the residence or place of his electoral area for registration. It is submitted that column 11 in Form 2 was inserted for preparation of data base for issuance of identity cards to the electors, there is no inconsistency in the press release dated 27-5-95 as published on 28-5-95 with regard to column 11 of the Form 2 prepared under rule 4 of the Electoral Rolls Rules, 1982 and the administrative order dated 27.5.95 issued vide the press release is the proper course so as to enable a person to become elector of any one of their electoral bodies, viz Union Parishad, Municipality and City Corporation on the basis of registration. The petitioner has not made out a case in the writ petition that he complied with the requirements of and filled up the Form 2 sitting at a different place from that of his permanent residence expressing his desire to be enrolled as voter before the issuance of the press release for getting the benefit of the decision given on this point in the other writ petition No. 1323 of 1995. The learned Additional Attorney-General has, however, not disputed the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the press release cannot have the retrospective effect but in this regard also he challenged the locus standi of the petitioner in maintaining the writ petition on the ground that he is not an aggrieved person. 

 In view of the fact that the petitioner has not made out a case that he attained the age of eighteen years after 1.1.95 and thus was debarred from being enrolled as voter in the electoral roll and that he filled up the form in terms of item 11 (Ka) and 11 (Kha) of the Form No. 11 before the press release was issued, we have no hesitation to hold that he is not an aggrieved person and hence has no locus standi to file this writ petition claiming the relief sought for.
